key_insight: Workspace Models shift expensive vision-language model (VLM) reasoning out of the robot’s online control loop and into training, learning a lightweight memory that focuses only on task-salient events. This makes long-horizon manipulation more efficient and less vulnerable to noise from full-history conditioning.
problem_solved: Robotic policies often need memory of past events, but feeding full histories into the policy can introduce spurious correlations and hurt performance. Existing memory methods can also be costly because they rely on VLM queries during inference.
method: Use computationally intensive VLM queries during training to identify which past observations/actions are truly salient for the task.
Train a lightweight workspace memory model that stores compressed, task-relevant information instead of raw full histories.
At inference time, rely on the learned memory to support long-term manipulation without expensive online VLM calls.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical path to scalable robot memory: better long-horizon behavior with lower latency and compute. It is especially useful for deployment settings where online VLM use is too slow or expensive.
